units.fit_note: Also lists research, analysis, images and writing improvement, and is conditional on the course. | Also permits images and writing improvement.

units.passage: Students are invited to use GAI platforms to help prepare for assignments and projects (e.g., to help with brainstorming or to see what a completed essay might look like).
units.why: 'Students are invited to use GAI platforms to help prepare for assignments and projects (e.g., to help with brainstorming ...)' welcomes AI for preparatory work, with brainstorming as the named example; that is P15 (brainstorming and exploring approaches), and the invitation is encouraging.

units.passage: (Low Risk) – In general, this is a productive use of generative AI tools.
units.why: Brainstorming ideas is 'a productive use of generative AI tools', a permitted use (P15).

units.passage: These tools can be valuable for brainstorming, drafting, and enhancing your understanding of the material.
units.why: "valuable for brainstorming, drafting, and enhancing your understanding" names brainstorming and drafting as good uses (P15).
units.fit_note: Also lists drafting and understanding the material, not only brainstorming. | Also names drafting and understanding course material.

units.passage: AI tools are great for inspiring ideas, exploring topics, and examining problems.
units.why: "AI tools are great for inspiring ideas, exploring topics, and examining problems" permits and encourages brainstorming and exploration, so P15.

units.passage: Generative AI may be used productively as a thinking partner to brainstorm topics and narrow the scope of your research question.
units.why: 'Generative AI may be used productively as a thinking partner to brainstorm topics' permits brainstorming, so P15.

units.passage: This course (or assignment) allows for the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) technologies as part of the research and preparation phase of the work, for example using these technologies to assist with research, generating ideas, creating summaries of topics, and developing drafts of text that are then used as an input to the work students do to generate a final assignment
units.why: The second sample statement allows AI "as part of the research and preparation phase", for ideas, summaries and drafts that feed the student's own work; nearest P15.
units.fit_note: Covers research, idea generation, topic summaries and draft text as input, limited to the preparation phase. | Covers research help, summaries and draft input as well as brainstorming.

units.passage: Students may use AI tools for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity) as outlined in the assignment instructions.
units.policy: Students may use AI tools for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity) as outlined in the assignment instructions.
units.why: Option 2 allows AI "for specific purposes (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, editing for clarity)", a narrow list of permitted uses; P15 fits brainstorming but outlining and editing also appear, so I note the fit.
units.fit_note: Also lists outlining and editing for clarity, and ties the allowed purposes to each assignment's instructions. Narrow list of permitted purposes also includes outlining and editing for clarity (writing support), not only brainstorming.

units.passage: Generative AI offers numerous ways to support your education, such as thinking through ideas, making study guides or practice problems, or providing help with understanding difficult concepts.
units.why: The same sentence lists 'thinking through ideas' as a way AI supports education, which is idea generation, so P15.

units.passage: In a policy brief, allow students to use AI to generate opposing viewpoints and an outline, but require their final text to be original and supported by peer-reviewed or canonical sources they locate independently.
units.why: Strategic example allows AI for 'opposing viewpoints and an outline' in a policy brief while requiring original final text: an instructor-designed permitted use of AI for brainstorming and exploring approaches (P15), designed in advance of the course.
units.fit_note: Example of a Strategic assignment, tied to writing a policy brief.

units.passage: Generate ideas, create project titles or outline a paper's structure.
units.why: The table column is headed "Good Practice" for brainstorming uses (A should, B may). The text recommends them while saying to check with the instructor first, so should.

units.passage: Use GenAI to enhance the phases of your work that don't directly assess your core learning (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, light editing
units.policy: Use GenAI to enhance the phases of your work that don't directly assess your core learning (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, light editing).
units.why: "Use GenAI to enhance the phases of your work that don't directly assess your core learning (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, light editing)" is a next-step recommendation (A should, B may). Should; B's policy keeps the examples.
units.fit_note: Also covers outlining and light editing, and ties the permission to which phases assess core learning. | Also covers light editing.

units.passage: brainstorming partner
units.why: Limited-use example: AI as a "brainstorming partner", P15.

units.passage: Drafting an outline to organize thoughts
units.why: "Drafting an outline to organize thoughts" is idea and structure exploration, P15 (A P18, B P15). P18 is for rules that separate prose from code; the sentence does not make that distinction.

units.passage: You may use GenAI tools for outlining, organizing and exploring ideas
units.why: Sample limited statement: AI for outlining and ideas if acknowledged and cited: P15.

units.passage: You may use AI for planning, idea development and research.
units.why: Sample 'AI Planning' statement permits AI for planning and idea development, P15.

units.passage: Explore alternative approaches to problem-solving.
units.why: 'Explore alternative approaches to problem-solving' permits exploring approaches (P15).

units.passage: You can, though, ask AI for ideas to get started, to make a completed assignment better, to give suggestions for how to improve, etc.
units.why: Students 'can, though, ask AI for ideas to get started' or to improve a finished assignment; ideas are P15, the improvement use goes beyond.
units.fit_note: Also allows AI feedback to improve a completed assignment.

units.passage: You are especially encouraged to use them for:
units.why: 'Brainstorming ideas for assignments' is a use students are 'especially encouraged' to make (P15).
units.fit_note: The list that follows (brainstorming, editing, lesson materials, practice examples) is coded in separate units.
